messages.content: You earned tokens by accurately copying fictional student records for five minutes, after an unpaid two-minute practice. Each correct row earned 20 tokens. You make five anonymous public goods decisions, each using the income earned in that clerical task. Each time you are grouped with three different people whom you have not previously met in this game. Each group member independently chooses how much of their own income to report to a common fund, from 0% to 100%. Income you hide is kept privately. The common fund is doubled and divided equally among all four members, including someone who puts in zero. Your round earnings are your income minus what you put in plus half the total amount the group reports. Others’ individual incomes are not disclosed before decisions. After each round, you see what the other three put in, the common fund and your resulting earnings. At the experiment’s end, one of the five rounds is chosen at random for payment. Each token is worth EUR 0.01. Give only your choice as a percentage of your own income, from 0 to 100.

You are participating in a laboratory experiment in Bucharest, Romania.
Your background: no additional individual background is supplied in these records.
Your clerical-task income is 180 tokens. This is the first round.
Choose the percentage of your income to report now; the part you hide remains yours. None of this round’s group choices has been revealed.

You are making a sender–receiver strategy in a new anonymous pair. A computer selects a number from 1 to 6 and assigns one person as sender and the other as receiver. The implemented role and number are not revealed to you in this strategy screen. Both people submit choices for both possible roles. As a sender you specify one integer message from 1 to 6 for each possible assigned number 1,2,3,4,5,6. Your message need not equal that number. The sender earns 100 tokens plus 20 tokens times the reported number, regardless of what the receiver does. A receiver can accept or reject the message without knowing the true number. Rejecting gives the receiver 50 tokens. Accepting gives 100 tokens if the message is accurate and 0 if inaccurate. At the end, the computer uses the relevant contingent choices for the assigned roles and number to determine payment. Each token is worth EUR 0.01. This stage’s choices do not change the payment from the earlier public goods game. Submit one complete six-number plan, as a JSON array in the order of assigned numbers 1 through 6. Every component must be an integer from 1 to 6; give no explanation.

You are participating in a laboratory experiment in Bucharest, Romania.
Your background: no additional individual background is supplied in these records.
In the earlier public goods game your earned income was 180 tokens. Your own five choices to report, expressed as percentages of that income in round order, were: 100%, 50%, 50%, 94.44444274902344%, 0%.
After your first choice, before first-round feedback, you answered that group members should have reported 100% of their income. You also answered two count questions about the other three; their exact count answers are not preserved in these records.
The earlier rounds did give you group feedback, but the exact other-player contributions and your displayed earnings are unavailable in these records; this does not mean you did not see them.
After completing all five rounds you rated these statements from 0(completely disagree)to 4(completely agree): “I felt that I had to be honest”=2; “I wanted to get as much money as possible for me”=2; “I felt that I had to contribute for the common good”=2. These were your earlier answers, before this strategy task.
Choose your complete sender message plan now, for all six possible assigned numbers.
